verdict.rationale: Render documents scaling features on the same platform and primitives: load-based autoscaling for 100x bursts, HA databases with read replicas, and a single render.yaml Blueprint that defines the whole architecture. That implies a developer can grow without switching platforms. However, no evidence explicitly claims a prototype-to-massive-scale continuity without rearchitecting, and nothing shows real large-scale outcomes. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party claim that the same APIs work from prototype to massive scale with no rearchitecture, documented scale limits or tiers, and independent or hands-on reports of apps scaling to large size on Render without migrating.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the same core APIs and primitives from prototype through massive scale, without rearchitecting or migrating platforms as usage grows

citations.quote: Load-based autoscaling that handles 100x traffic bursts and beyond
Deploy fully-managed databases with point-in-time recovery, read replicas, and high availability.
Define, deploy, and version your entire architecture with a single YAML file.
Deploy reliable agents and background processes at scale, without wiring up queues, workers, and retry logic.
Render (https://render.com) is a cloud application platform for deploying, securing, and scaling applications
they support distributed Elixir out of the box as well as autoscaling
